high.title: A Paradox Is Opening a Major Opportunity in the Stock Market — Where Is Money Flowing?
high.summary:
July 2026 proved a brutal month for Vietnamese equity investors. The VN-Index briefly dipped to near the 1,650-point level before closing the month down approximately 7% — a selloff severe enough that the head of billion-dollar foreign fund Pyn Elite Fund described it as "Horrible July." The decline is particularly paradoxical given that Q2 2026 earnings season delivered broadly positive surprises: FiinGroup data through July 29 shows aggregate post-tax profit for 672 of 1,525 listed companies (representing ~39% of total market cap) grew 25.6% year-on-year. Non-financial corporates led with +36.1% profit growth, while the financial sector lagged at +10.7%. Several blue-chip non-financials — including Vinhomes, Mobile World (MWG), and FPT — reported record profits. **For fund managers, the disconnect between strong fundamentals and sharp price declines warrants close attention.** This divergence may signal that selling pressure is macro/sentiment-driven (USD strength, foreign outflows, risk-off), rather than earnings-based, potentially creating a value entry point. Watch foreign net flows and VND stability as key triggers for a reversal.

---

high.title: Overnight Interbank Rate Drops to 0.7% in Late July; SBV Net Injects VND 12.3 Trillion via OMO
high.summary: During the week of July 27–31, the State Bank of Vietnam (SBV) shifted to a net injection stance on the open market operations (OMO) channel, pumping a net VND 12,322.94 billion into the banking system via collateralized securities. The SBV offered VND 61,000 billion across tenors of 7, 42, 63, and 91 days at a steady rate of 4.5% per annum, with VND 48,341.63 billion successfully bid. Outstanding OMO balances on the collateral channel reached VND 172,530.36 billion. No treasury bills were issued during the week. As a result, overnight interbank rates fell to just 0.7%, signaling ample system liquidity. **Key implications:** The ultra-low overnight rate and net OMO injection confirm that the SBV is actively supporting liquidity conditions — a dovish near-term signal for VND money markets. Abundant liquidity could weigh on short-end government bond yields and reduce upward pressure on the VND, as banks have less incentive to bid aggressively for funds. Traders should monitor whether the SBV sustains this injection posture into August or pivots back to absorption if FX pressures re-emerge.

high.title: Bank Deposit Rates on August 3: LPBank Raises Rates Across Multiple Tenors — Now Second Highest in Market
high.summary: In the first week of August, LPBank enacted a notable upward revision to deposit rates across multiple tenors — the first meaningful adjustment after an extended period of rate stability. Effective August 3, LPBank raised its 6-month and 9-month rates from 6.8% to 7.1% p.a., its 12-month rate from 6.9% to 7.3% p.a., and its 18-month rate from 6.95% to 7.25% p.a. This positions LPBank as the second-highest rate-offering bank in the market for the 12-month tenor, behind only ACB, which leads at 7.8% p.a. for 12 months (with 7.6% and 7.7% for 6- and 9-month terms respectively). Other notable rates: Saigonbank at 7.2%, Bac A Bank at 7.1%, and MBV, VCBNeo, PGBank, and VIB all at 7.0%. **Key implications:** The upward move by LPBank — a mid-sized bank — signals that competition for retail deposits is intensifying despite the system's broadly loose liquidity. Rising deposit rates at the margin could eventually push up lending rates and government bond yields at the short-to-medium end. This divergence between system-level liquidity (ample per interbank data) and individual bank rate competition warrants close monitoring, as it may reflect idiosyncratic funding pressures at select institutions.

high.title: Billions of USD Waiting to Flow into Vietnamese Securities — Multiple Stocks Forecast to Attract Strong Capital Inflows
high.summary:
This is a pivotal development for Vietnamese capital markets. On **August 21, 2026**, FTSE Russell is scheduled to officially announce the constituent stocks included in the **FTSE Global Equity Index Series (FTSE GEIS)** for emerging markets, effective **September 21, 2026** — marking Vietnam's formal entry into the FTSE EM index universe.

FTSE estimates Vietnam's upgrade could attract approximately **USD 6 billion** in combined active and passive fund flows. ETFs tracking the FTSE index alone are projected to deploy roughly **USD 1.5 billion** over a 12-month horizon. In the base case for the September 2026 rebalancing, MB Securities (MBS) estimates **~USD 150 million in ETF inflows** concentrated in large-cap names.

Approximately **30 stocks** are expected to be included in the FTSE GEIS basket. VIC (Vingroup) is forecast to be the largest beneficiary, with estimated net buying of **~USD 46.4 million** (~1.19% of its market cap).

high.title: BIDV Bank's Latest Deposit Interest Rates for August 2026
high.summary:
BIDV, one of Vietnam's four largest state-owned commercial banks, has published its official deposit rate schedule for August 2026. Key rate levels are as follows: short-term deposits (1–5 months) are capped at **4.75%/year**, in line with the SBV's regulatory ceiling on sub-6-month deposits. Medium-term deposits (6–11 months) are offered at **6.6%/year**, while all long-term tenors from 12 to 36 months are uniformly priced at **6.8%/year** — the highest published rate in the online schedule. Online deposits continue to offer a premium over counter deposits across most tenors. USD deposits remain at **0%/year**, reinforcing the de-dollarization policy stance maintained by the SBV. The 4.75% cap on short-term VND deposits is a critical policy anchor, signaling that the SBV has not loosened its monetary stance. For bond investors, the 6.6–6.8% deposit rate corridor sets a de facto floor for short-to-medium government bond yield expectations. FX traders should note that the zero-rate USD policy continues to discourage domestic USD hoarding and supports VND stability. Watch for any future changes to the 6-month deposit ceiling as a leading indicator of SBV policy direction.

---

medium.title: Vietnamese Equities Enter a Month with Historically High Probability of Gains — Which Stock Groups Could Attract Capital?
medium.summary: According to Nguyen The Minh, Head of Investment Banking at An Binh Securities (ABS), historical data shows August is seasonally one of the stronger months for the VN-Index, with average gains exceeding 2%, and mid- and small-cap stocks typically outperforming. On the global macro front, the US Federal Reserve held the federal funds rate steady at 3.50–3.75% at its July meeting — the fifth consecutive pause — in line with market expectations. However, three FOMC members dissented in favor of a 25bp hike, keeping the door open for a rate increase as early as September 2026. **This is material for VND traders:** a potential Fed hike in September would likely strengthen the USD, adding depreciation pressure on VND and potentially complicating SBV's exchange rate management heading into Q4. Investors should monitor the August FOMC communications closely alongside Vietnam's trade balance data.

medium.title: Vietnam Stock Market Eyes Key September Event — What Do Experts Say?
medium.summary: On August 21, 2026, FTSE Russell is scheduled to officially announce the constituent stocks included in the FTSE Global Equity Index Series (FTSE GEIS) Emerging Markets segment, effective September 21, 2026. FTSE estimates Vietnam's upgrade from Frontier to Emerging Market status could attract approximately USD 6 billion in total inflows from active and passive funds, with ETFs tracking the FTSE index expected to deploy around USD 1.5 billion over a phased one-year period. VinaCapital's Senior Investment Director Dinh Duc Minh cautioned that market impact is likely to materialize gradually rather than as an immediate shock. **For FX and bond investors, this is a pivotal capital flow event:** USD 6 billion in foreign inflows — even phased — would be meaningfully supportive of VND and could compress government bond yields as foreign demand for local assets rises. However, the phased nature of ETF rebalancing means the VND/USD impact may be spread over 12 months. Watch August 21 for the official constituent list as a near-term market catalyst.

medium.title: VN-Index "Well-Positioned" to Break 1,800 Points — Brokerages Identify Stocks with Unique Narratives and Attractive Valuations
medium.summary:
Vietnam's stock market endured a volatile July 2026, with liquidity remaining persistently low, reflecting cautious investor sentiment and a "wait-and-see" posture among domestic money flows. The hardest-hit sectors included securities, real estate, banking, and technology. Heading into August, Agriseco Research expects the **VN-Index to recover toward the 1,800-point level** after forming a short-term base near **1,651 points**. Key support drivers cited include economic growth stimulus policies, accelerated public investment disbursement, FDI attraction measures, and attractive valuations with market P/E at approximately **11.7x — below the 5-year historical average**. However, upside risks are tempered by inflation pressures, continued **net foreign selling**, and global geopolitical uncertainty. For fund managers, the combination of depressed valuations, an imminent FTSE upgrade catalyst, and policy support suggests a constructive medium-term setup, though near-term foreign outflow dynamics warrant close monitoring for VND impact.

---

medium.title: HDBank Plans 30% Total Dividend and Bonus Share Issuance
medium.summary: Ho Chi Minh City Development Bank (HDBank, ticker: HDB) is seeking shareholder approval via written ballot (August 3–14, 2026) for a plan to distribute a **25% stock dividend** from 2025 retained earnings, plus an additional **5% bonus share issuance** from the statutory capital reserve fund — totaling a **30% capital increase**. This involves issuing up to approximately 1.5 billion new shares. While this is a corporate action rather than a macro event, large-scale share issuances by banking sector constituents can impact the VN-Index's weighting and sector liquidity. Equity investors should monitor the ex-dividend date and potential dilution effects on HDB's share price and book value per share.

medium.title: Military Bank (MB) to Pay 15% Stock Dividend with August 12 Record Date
medium.summary: MB Bank (ticker: MBB, HoSE) has set **August 12, 2026** as the record date for a **15% stock dividend**, involving the issuance of over 1.2 billion new shares (face value: ~VND 12,083 billion) sourced from 2025 undistributed profits. Simultaneously, MB will also finalize the shareholder list for a separate public offering of ~805.5 million shares at a 10:1 rights ratio, following regulatory approval from the State Securities Commission (SSC) on July 31, 2026. As MBB is one of the largest banking stocks by market capitalization on HoSE, this dual capital action — stock dividend plus rights offering — is relevant for VN-Index index trackers and banking sector investors, particularly regarding post-issuance dilution and potential index rebalancing impacts.

medium.title: Agribank's Latest Deposit Interest Rates for August 2026: What Is the Highest Rate?
medium.summary: Agribank — one of Vietnam's four largest state-owned commercial banks — has held its deposit rate schedule unchanged entering August 2026, maintaining the same rate structure as the prior month. Counter deposit rates range from 0.2% per annum (demand/current accounts) up to a peak of **6.0% p.a. for 24-month tenors**. Key benchmarks include: 1–2 month at 2.6%, 3–5 month at 2.9%, 6–11 month at 4.0%, and 12–18 month tenors clustered at 5.9%. Online savings rates continue to be offered at a premium above counter rates. The stability in Agribank's rates signals that the broader Vietnamese banking system deposit rate environment remains steady, with no immediate pressure from the SBV to adjust policy. For bond market participants, the 6% ceiling on 24-month bank deposits provides a useful reference anchor for short-to-medium duration government bond yield expectations. Continued rate stability suggests the SBV is comfortable with current monetary conditions.
